ask.description: What the plan gate of a run asks, a text template over `.Unit` (the unit as people read it) and `.Facts` (the unit's facts by name, such as `{{index .Facts "session.name"}}`); its summary when absent.

drafts.description: The drafts the workflow's steps and turns propose.

withdraw.description: When an open draft the workflow proposed is withdrawn.

reason.description: The reason the withdrawn draft stores.

rule.description: A rule tried before when, in order, that withdraws with a reason of its own.

reason.description: The reason the draft the rule withdraws stores.

when.description: When the rule withdraws an open draft the workflow proposed, over the unit's facts and the draft's. Required.
When an open draft the workflow proposed is withdrawn, over the unit's facts and the draft's.

enabled.description: false ships the workflow off: it plans nothing until workflows.<name>.enabled = true in the config turns it on.

gates.description: The gates its runs and drafts open.

approval.description: The approval of its gates: a rule applies to the kinds its when pins gate.kind to, else to draft gates alone when it reads a draft's facts, else to every kind; what no rule or mode here decides, gates.toml's [approval] does.

mode.description: The mode of every kind of gate when no rule holds; left out, gates.toml's default of the kind.

rule.description: A rule; the first whose when holds gives the mode.

when.description: When the rule applies to a gate.

window.description: With mode delay only: how long a person has to stop the gate's consequence.
With mode delay only: how long a person has to stop the gate's consequence.

drafts_wait.description: Every draft the workflow proposes waits for a person: no approval rule of its own or of the configuration releases it.

withdraw.description: When an open gate the workflow's gate.open opened on a unit no longer stands: the engine supersedes it at the start of a sweep and records gate_withdrawn on its task with the reason, so a step whose subject is gone never waits for you to dismiss it.

reason.description: Why the gate was withdrawn, as its task's timeline shows it.

when.description: When an open gate the workflow opened is withdrawn, over its unit's facts; it may read no untrusted fact, since a withdrawal closes a gate that waits on you. Required.

key.description: The facts forming the idempotency key, by default <slot>.fingerprint: a key that ran or was dismissed is not planned again. A workflow with trigger.on may add trigger.event.id, so each event plans its own run.

limits.description: How many runs the workflow may take.

cooldown.description: The least time between runs on one unit.

per_day.description: Runs per local day; 0 is no limit.

per_run.description: Runs per evaluation; 0 is no limit.

per_unit_per_day.description: Runs on one unit per local day; 0 is no limit.

additionalProperties.description: The fact whose value the mark stores.

marks.description: Mark name to fact, stored when a run is done or dismissed, which handled() reads.

observe.description: Plans items pending and never runs them by itself; a person applies an item by hand.

outbox.description: How the Outbox heads the group of the drafts the workflow proposed.

about.description: One line under the title on when the workflow drafts them, such as "Drafted when a conversation where you asked something goes quiet."

title.description: The group's title, what the drafts are for, such as "Ask who hasn't answered"; the summary when absent.

provider.description: The provider of the units it matches. Required.

step.description: A step the run takes, in order. Required: at least one.

reason.description: The reason the dismissed turn records.
The reason the refused answer records.

due.description: When the round is due: plan, when the unit's plan holds it due; when, whenever the workflow's when matches, as a round to retry what a failed round left, whatever the plan holds.

intent.description: The intent whose turn starts; it must serve the unit. Required.

open_question.description: What an open question of the intent's newest turn does to a round of the unit's plan: hold waits for its answer; replace_if_moved runs a round planned on a head other than the one the question was asked on, which replaces the asked turn, supersedes its gate and carries the question in the new turn's history. An answer on its way holds the round either way.

runner.description: How the turn runs, one of the intent's runners; by default its first.

stage.description: The pass over the unit: its first, or one after; empty is the one the unit's plan holds due, one after before its first.

delivery.description: How the draft posts, a delivery the plugin that posts it declares; empty is that plugin's default delivery.

ended.description: What a draft withdrawn as its task ended does while that task stays ended: hold the workflow's proposals of no task or of that task, or hold them for repeat_after like any settled draft.

items.description: Which of the unit's items the draft lists.

per.description: One draft per unit, or one per person it waits on.

purpose.description: What the draft is for, such as nudge or close. Required.

reaction.description: The emoji name, with delivery reaction.

repeat_after.description: The least time after a settled draft of the same person before another: a duration, or a config.* duration fact such as config.drafts.repeat_after.

repeat_after_sent.description: The same after a sent draft, by default repeat_after: a duration, a config.* duration fact, or forever.

target.description: Where the draft posts: on the unit, on each item, or, with per = "person", in the direct conversation between you and the person it is to; an intent's help.target is free text.

text.description: The template of the draft's text, beside the manifest, rendered in the language of the draft's conversation.

to.description: Whom of the people the items wait on the draft addresses: all of them, those its unit's plugin knows are members of the conversation it posts on, or those it knows are not; a person whose membership the plugin cannot tell is left out of both.

why.description: The template of why the draft is proposed, beside the manifest, rendered in the user's language over the same data as the text; a workflow with no such file proposes with no why.

prompt.description: The classification's prompt, beside the manifest.

schema.description: The JSON schema of its answer, beside the manifest.

with.description: A list fact of task ids, such as task.candidates, whose tasks the prompt reads beside the unit: the prompt is then a template over .Facts, the unit's facts, .Task, the unit's own task when it is one, and .Tasks, the listed tasks in order, each with .ID, .Title, .Notes and .Items, a few of its items' summaries. Every untrusted value is inside this call's markers, .Begin and .End, which carry the code .Nonce. The output is cached by what the prompt reads of the unit's task and the listed tasks (ids, titles, notes, item summaries) and by the prompt and the schema, so a write that changes none of them, such as opening a task, keeps it, and an edit of the prompt or the schema asks again; the unit's facts a prompt prints through .Facts are not part of the key, and with a unit that is not a task the key holds the unit's fingerprint too. Only a reader that names it reads it. An empty list runs nothing.

text.description: The template of the notification's text, beside the manifest: `.Workflow`, `.Unit` and `.Facts`.

by.description: With a verb whose handler is promise, the time the task is promised by: HH:MM, YYYY-MM-DD or RFC 3339; empty clears it.

each.description: With `task` naming a list fact, `true` runs the verb with every task the list names, in order, each opening its own gate where the verb is gated, so one that waits for you does not hold back the rest; else the verb runs with the first.

on.description: With a verb whose handler is waiting, the people the task waits on, comma-separated.

on_activity.description: With a verb whose handler is schedule, `true` returns the task on new activity on its unit.

resurface.description: With a verb whose handler is waiting, the date the task resurfaces: RFC 3339 or YYYY-MM-DD.

set.description: With a verb whose handler is context, the contexts, comma-separated; with area, the area.

task.description: With a verb whose handler is merge, split, relate or unrelate, the fact that names the other task: a string fact holding its id, or a list fact whose first element does, such as task.link_target_tasks, or a classify output, such as classify.<workflow>.task, which no fact table declares before it runs; the step is refused while it names none.

until.description: With a verb whose handler is schedule, the date the task returns: RFC 3339 or YYYY-MM-DD.

verb.description: The verb of tasks.toml run on the task, one whose by.workflow lets a workflow run it. Required.

name.description: The gate, of gates.toml, the step opens. Required.

prop.description: The property, of tasks.toml, the step sets. Required.

value.description: The value, written as its type reads it: an enum's value, a date as YYYY-MM-DD or as a duration after now such as +2d, a duration, a list comma-separated. Required.

summary.description: One line, what the workflow does; its plan items' description. Required.

trigger.description: What plans the workflow: on or schedule; absent, every sweep.

actors.description: With on, the actors whose verb events plan it (person, workflow, agent, plugin); every actor when absent.

depth.description: With on, the longest chain of workflows triggering each other the workflow may close: an event a chain of that many workflows caused plans it no more, and a workflow already in an event's chain never runs on it. 1 to 5.

on.description: The event kinds the workflow reacts to: the loop's, the plugins', task.woke (a task's wake matched) and verb_<verb>, a verb of tasks.toml run on a task by anyone, a workflow included; the last two with provider task.

schedule.description: A cron schedule, in local time.

when.description: The match condition, over the unit's facts, the trigger's and config.*. Required.
